recipes.title: Chat with PDF documents offline
recipes.description: Prepare models before disconnecting, choose local processing at every stage, and inspect cited passages. These documented configurations have not been installed or quality-benchmarked in this research pass.

picks.label: Folder-based document collections
picks.reason: LocalDocs indexes local text snippets and exposes source references.
picks.tradeoff: Disable off-device embedding, use a local chat model and note the unverified maintenance status.

picks.label: Attach documents to a local chat
picks.reason: Supports PDF attachments with local processing and a documented offline workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Long files use retrieval; cloud features and model downloads are separate online operations.

picks.label: Configurable document workspaces
picks.reason: Combines PDF ingestion with selectable local models, embeddings and storage.
picks.tradeoff: All selected providers must stay local; first-use model downloads and context limits need preparation.

recipes.title: Reduce steady noise in an audio recording
recipes.description: Compare two documented noise-profile workflows for recorded material. Judge artifacts against the original recording; these entries do not establish live microphone suppression or a measured quality winner.

picks.label: Focused free editing workflow
picks.reason: Provides a noise-profile effect for steady hum, hiss and similar backgrounds.
picks.tradeoff: Needs a noise-only sample and is unsuitable for many irregular noises.

picks.label: Inside an existing multitrack project
picks.reason: The included ReaFIR effect offers profile-based subtraction.
picks.tradeoff: Paid workstation licensing and effect setup are additional considerations.

recipes.title: Choose an editor for layered images and retouching
recipes.description: Start with the kind of artwork and editable files you must deliver; painting, photo retouching and vector work need different strengths.

picks.label: Photoshop document handoff
picks.reason: Layered compositing and retouching fit a workflow that exchanges editable Photoshop documents.
picks.tradeoff: Subscription and cloud-feature allowances add cost; test required plug-ins and file round trips.

picks.label: Combined design application
picks.reason: Pixel, vector and layout studios suit a mixed design workflow with a free core application.
picks.tradeoff: A Canva account is required and optional AI features depend on paid plans; verify client file exchange.

picks.label: Open-source raster editing
picks.reason: A capable candidate for local raster editing when an open-source workflow matters.
picks.tradeoff: Check the exact adjustment, color-management and Photoshop interchange requirements.

picks.label: Painting and illustration
picks.reason: Brush-focused drawing tools suit illustration and digital painting.
picks.tradeoff: A painting workflow is different from photographic catalog management or a full Photoshop handoff.

recipes.title: Choose a RAW photo development workflow
recipes.description: Evaluate representative camera files, image organization, tethering needs and the full licensing model before selecting a converter.

picks.label: Local catalog and batch editing
picks.reason: Combines a local photo catalog with repeatable RAW development.
picks.tradeoff: A subscription is required, and Classic uses a different storage model from cloud-centered Lightroom.

picks.label: Tethered studio work
picks.reason: Tethered capture and controlled color editing suit supported studio camera setups.
picks.tradeoff: Check camera support and plan differences; a perpetual license has different update rights.

picks.label: Optical corrections with perpetual licensing
picks.reason: Camera/lens corrections and RAW processing make it a candidate for a purchased-version workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Test exact camera and lens support, GPU requirements and edition-specific features.

picks.label: Open-source photographic workflow
picks.reason: Non-destructive RAW processing suits a local open-source photo workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Its processing model and learning curve differ from commercial editors; test your own images.

picks.label: Detailed RAW development
picks.reason: A useful candidate for detailed RAW conversion and adjustment.
picks.tradeoff: Choose a separate organizational workflow when its catalog features do not match your archive.

recipes.title: Choose a video editor for real project delivery
recipes.description: Use representative footage and required export formats; timeline compatibility, color work and hardware matter more than a universal ranking.

picks.label: Editing with color and finishing
picks.reason: A candidate when editing, color and finishing need a coordinated production workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Free and Studio capabilities differ, and GPU, codec and platform support need checking.

picks.label: Adobe timeline exchange
picks.reason: Fits teams that deliver editable Premiere projects and connect to Adobe post-production tools.
picks.tradeoff: Subscription and project-sized CPU, GPU and storage needs add cost.

picks.label: Open-source nonlinear editing
picks.reason: A general timeline editor for users who want an open-source editing workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Evaluate effects, proxy behavior and export results using the intended footage.

picks.label: Independent desktop editing
picks.reason: A candidate for straightforward editing and media workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Complex collaboration and project exchange may require a different editor.

recipes.title: Choose tools for motion graphics and visual effects
recipes.description: Separate animated design, node compositing and three-dimensional scene creation before comparing applications.

picks.label: Layered motion design
picks.reason: Keyframed layers, animated text and tracking suit motion-design compositions.
picks.tradeoff: Subscription, preview memory and render time matter; a video editor is still useful for final assembly.

picks.label: Node-based compositing
picks.reason: A node workflow suits assembling image operations into a visual effects graph.
picks.tradeoff: Check the required effects, plug-ins and production maintenance needs.

picks.label: Three-dimensional scenes and rendering
picks.reason: Use it when the shot needs models, animation, rendered scenes and compositing in one package.
picks.tradeoff: Learning a 3D production environment can be disproportionate for a simple title animation.

recipes.title: Choose a desktop office suite
recipes.description: Compare required document fidelity, spreadsheet features, collaboration rules and supported operating systems using real files.

picks.label: Microsoft desktop compatibility
picks.reason: Choose when the work depends on Microsoft desktop application features and editable Office handoffs.
picks.tradeoff: Use a plan that includes installed apps; recurring cost and Windows/Mac differences remain.

picks.label: Open-source local office work
picks.reason: A full local office suite is useful when open formats and independent desktop editing are priorities.
picks.tradeoff: Complex Office documents, macros and layouts need file-by-file compatibility checks.

picks.label: Office-format editing workflow
picks.reason: A candidate for editing familiar document, spreadsheet and presentation formats on the desktop.
picks.tradeoff: Confirm required macros, accessibility and complex document features before replacing an established suite.

recipes.title: Edit PDFs or turn scanned pages into searchable documents
recipes.description: Identify whether the job is editing existing content, recognizing scans, rearranging pages or running repeated document transformations.

picks.label: Broad PDF editing workflow
picks.reason: Combines PDF editing, conversion and signing for Acrobat-based document exchange.
picks.tradeoff: Requires a subscription; optional AI and service features can have separate entitlements.

picks.label: OCR-focused conversion
picks.reason: A candidate when converting scanned layouts into searchable or editable documents is the main task.
picks.tradeoff: Mac and Windows editions differ; automated CLI/RPA use has separate license conditions.

picks.label: Repeatable searchable-PDF processing
picks.reason: Adds recognition to PDF workflows when a command-line pipeline is appropriate.
picks.tradeoff: It does not provide a general visual editor for the original page content.

picks.label: Page organization
picks.reason: Focused page arrangement can be sufficient for joining, reordering or splitting documents.
picks.tradeoff: Choose another tool for OCR or editing text inside a page.

picks.label: Many PDF operations in one interface
picks.reason: A candidate for a broader set of document transformations through one interface.
picks.tradeoff: Deployment, edition and component licensing need review; assess any server exposure.

recipes.title: Explore business data and build visual reports
recipes.description: Compare local authoring separately from publishing and team distribution, because those capabilities often have different licenses.

picks.label: Free Windows report authoring
picks.reason: Build and inspect local Power BI data models and report pages without a paid desktop authoring license.
picks.tradeoff: Windows-only desktop; organizational publishing and service sharing require separate entitlements.

picks.label: Visual exploration on Windows or Mac
picks.reason: The current Free Edition supports local visualization and database/file analysis.
picks.tradeoff: Free Edition is for the user’s own internal analysis: no exchange of Tableau content, client outputs or Cloud/Server access; registration and possible reconnection apply.

picks.label: Visual analytical pipelines
picks.reason: Graphical workflows suit exploratory data analysis and modeling.
picks.tradeoff: It serves a different purpose from enterprise dashboard publishing and governed report distribution.

picks.label: Programmable and reproducible analysis
picks.reason: Notebooks combine code, explanations and plots for custom data work.
picks.tradeoff: Requires programming and an explicit process for sharing or deploying interactive reports.

recipes.title: Choose a numerical or symbolic computing environment
recipes.description: Begin with existing code, mathematical methods and required toolboxes; symbolic algebra and numerical engineering are related but distinct needs.

picks.label: Established engineering toolchain
picks.reason: Fits laboratories, courses and engineering code that require MATLAB and specific toolboxes.
picks.tradeoff: Toolboxes and deployment products can add licenses; Mac and Linux capabilities require checking.

picks.label: Open-source numerical scripting
picks.reason: A candidate for numerical work and compatible portions of MATLAB-style code.
picks.tradeoff: Proprietary toolbox behavior and complete MATLAB compatibility are not guaranteed.

picks.label: Integrated symbolic notebooks
picks.reason: Combines symbolic mathematics, numerical evaluation and interactive technical documents.
picks.tradeoff: Paid use-class terms and optional online-service entitlements apply.

picks.label: Open-source mathematical environment
picks.reason: Brings several mathematical systems into a programmable open-source workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Installation and differences between underlying systems can require more setup.

picks.label: Focused symbolic algebra
picks.reason: A candidate for symbolic manipulation without a full commercial technical-computing subscription.
picks.tradeoff: Compare notebook, plotting and specialized function needs separately.

recipes.title: Choose CAD for drawings, parametric parts or manufacturing
recipes.description: Pick by the deliverable: a DWG drawing set, a parametric model, a scripted shape or a manufacturing workflow.

picks.label: DWG production drafting
picks.reason: Fits projects with AutoCAD-specific drawings, conventions and tooling.
picks.tradeoff: Subscription or Flex cost and Windows/Mac toolset differences matter.

picks.label: Focused two-dimensional drafting
picks.reason: A candidate when precise 2D drawings are the main output.
picks.tradeoff: Community and Professional editions differ; verify required file formats and tools.

picks.label: Connected design and CAM
picks.reason: Combines product modeling with manufacturing preparation in one connected workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Personal-use eligibility is restricted, and extensions or commercial use can require payment.

picks.label: Open-source parametric modeling
picks.reason: Fits a desktop workflow that values editable parametric models and an open-source environment.
picks.tradeoff: Validate workbench maturity, geometry and exported files against the intended production process.

picks.label: Programmatic solid geometry
picks.reason: Useful when repeatable geometric design is best expressed as code and parameters.
picks.tradeoff: Its script-based workflow is less suited to direct freeform sculpting or drafting.

recipes.title: Automate repeated Windows desktop tasks
recipes.description: Choose between visual flows, scriptable input and tested automation; account for UI changes and error recovery.

picks.label: Visual application workflows
picks.reason: Records and composes desktop or browser actions with a Microsoft automation environment.
picks.tradeoff: Included attended use has limits; sharing, cloud orchestration and unattended runs need appropriate licenses.

picks.label: Custom shortcuts and input scripts
picks.reason: Fits keyboard shortcuts, text automation and small custom Windows scripts.
picks.tradeoff: Scripts need maintenance and explicit handling of focus, timing and application changes.

picks.label: Structured automation suites
picks.reason: A keyword-driven framework suits repeatable flows with reusable libraries and reports.
picks.tradeoff: Library selection and a development environment add setup compared with a recorded desktop flow.

recipes.title: Run Windows applications on a Mac
recipes.description: Verify the Mac CPU architecture, guest operating system and the actual application before choosing a VM product.

picks.label: Integrated Mac desktop workflow
picks.reason: Guided guest setup and desktop integration suit frequent use of supported Windows applications.
picks.tradeoff: Paid product; Windows licensing is separate, and Apple-silicon guest/application limitations remain.

picks.label: No-charge Fusion route
picks.reason: Fusion is the Mac member of VMware’s currently free desktop hypervisor family.
picks.tradeoff: Broadcom account downloads and guest support checks are required; Workstation is the separate Windows/Linux host product.

picks.label: Open-source Mac virtualization interface
picks.reason: A candidate for managing supported virtualized or emulated operating systems on a Mac.
picks.tradeoff: Virtualization and cross-architecture emulation have different performance and compatibility tradeoffs.

recipes.title: Prepare editable vector artwork and page layouts for collaborators
recipes.description: The requested delivery format and publication structure should determine whether you need vector illustration, typesetting or a combined design app.

picks.label: Native Illustrator vector delivery
picks.reason: Fits scalable artwork when collaborators specifically require Illustrator files and workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Subscription; document exchange still needs testing for fonts and effects.

picks.label: Structured publication production
picks.reason: Fits books, magazines and multipage publications requiring InDesign handoff.
picks.tradeoff: Subscription and publication training add cost, and linked assets must be managed.

picks.label: Combined vector and layout work
picks.reason: Offers vector, pixel and layout studios in one free-core application.
picks.tradeoff: Requires a Canva account and verification of the requested interchange formats.

picks.label: Open-source SVG artwork
picks.reason: A candidate for scalable vector drawings centered on SVG workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Complex Illustrator-specific effects and long-document typesetting are different requirements.

picks.label: Open-source page layout
picks.reason: A candidate for desktop publishing when a local open-source workflow is preferred.
picks.tradeoff: Evaluate typography, print settings and handoff requirements on the actual publication.

recipes.title: Analyze microscopy slides and three-dimensional scans
recipes.description: Choose by image type and analysis method: interactive segmentation, large-slide annotation, repeatable measurement pipelines or learned classification.

picks.label: Extensible volume workspace
picks.reason: Combines volumetric visualization, segmentation, registration and extensions in one shared environment.
picks.tradeoff: Validate the selected extensions and analysis method for the research workflow; the application does not establish clinical suitability.

picks.label: Focused volume segmentation
picks.reason: Linked orthogonal views and manual or active-contour segmentation suit tracing structures through image volumes.
picks.tradeoff: Its focused toolset offers fewer general-purpose extensions than 3D Slicer; stable and beta packages differ.

picks.label: Whole-slide annotations
picks.reason: Whole-slide viewing, object measurements and interactive classifiers suit microscopy-slide workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Validate classifiers and measurements on representative images; upstream specifies research use.

picks.label: Repeatable batch measurements
picks.reason: Explicit processing pipelines apply the same measurement sequence to many biological images.
picks.tradeoff: Good pipelines still need segmentation tuning and quality checks; Linux uses a separate source-installation route.

picks.label: Interactive image classification
picks.reason: Brush labels train pixel and object classifiers without writing a model-training program.
picks.tradeoff: Training examples determine the result, and GPU packages add hardware and licensing requirements.

recipes.title: Visualize molecules, crystals and particle simulations
recipes.description: Match the viewer to the data: molecular structures and maps, crystallographic densities, teaching demonstrations or particle trajectories.

picks.label: Molecular models with density maps
picks.reason: Combines molecular and volume visualization with commands and extension packages for structural-biology workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Noncommercial and commercial use have different terms; published source is not under an unrestricted open-source license.

picks.label: Scripted molecular figures
picks.reason: Scriptable scenes and molecular representations suit repeatable molecular illustrations.
picks.tradeoff: Commercial application bundles and permissively licensed source have different distribution and support terms.

picks.label: Portable chemistry demonstrations
picks.reason: Java desktop viewing and the related JSmol browser workflow support interactive molecular teaching.
picks.tradeoff: The desktop JAR requires Java; browser embedding is a separate deployment task.

picks.label: Crystals and volume densities
picks.reason: Crystal, polyhedral and isosurface views help inspect structures and density data together.
picks.tradeoff: The redistribution license is restrictive; current terms allow business use at no cost only until business-license conditions are established.

picks.label: Particle and atomistic trajectories
picks.reason: Pipeline-based particle analysis connects structural measurements with simulation visualization.
picks.tradeoff: Basic and Pro expose different modifiers and automation features; large trajectories need suitable resources.

recipes.title: Plot measurements, fit curves and explore mathematics
recipes.description: Choose an interactive plotting application, a scriptable figure generator, a specialist fitter or a broader mathematical environment.

picks.label: Graphical experimental analysis
picks.reason: Worksheets, plots, fitting, data import and digitization support a graphical measurement-analysis workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Notebook backends require separate runtimes; verify fitting models and imported units.

picks.label: Versionable plotting scripts
picks.reason: A compact plotting language produces repeatable two- and three-dimensional figures in automated workflows.
picks.tradeoff: The command language and terminal-specific output settings require learning.

picks.label: Peak and curve fitting
picks.reason: Interactive model construction and fitting tools suit overlapping peaks and experimental curves.
picks.tradeoff: Its published desktop binaries are older than its source release; assess packaging and model assumptions.

picks.label: Numerical engineering and Xcos
picks.reason: Matrix calculations, visualization and block-diagram simulation share one numerical environment.
picks.tradeoff: MATLAB language and toolbox compatibility are incomplete; check each external module.

picks.label: Symbolic and algebraic exploration
picks.reason: A Python-based interface brings algebra, number theory and numerical packages into one mathematical system.
picks.tradeoff: The dependency stack is substantial, and current Windows usage goes through WSL or containers.

recipes.title: Choose a simulation workflow for an engineering problem
recipes.description: Start with the physics and model representation; these tools serve different stages and are often complementary.

picks.label: Equation-based system models
picks.reason: Modelica models and simulation tools suit coupled dynamic systems and reusable component models.
picks.tradeoff: Library compatibility, solver settings and initialization need validation for the chosen model.

picks.label: Interactive electronics learning
picks.reason: A visual real-time circuit environment supports analog, digital and selected microcontroller experiments.
picks.tradeoff: Device models and simulator approximations limit fidelity; check version-specific component support.

picks.label: Biomechanics finite elements
picks.reason: Nonlinear materials and coupled physics focus on biomechanics and biophysics models, with FEBio Studio for model work.
picks.tradeoff: A specialist solver requires validated material models and boundary conditions; source and binary licenses differ.

picks.label: Computational fluid dynamics
picks.reason: The Foundation distribution supplies extensible solvers and utilities for continuum and fluid simulations.
picks.tradeoff: Mesh quality, boundary conditions and solver selection require expertise; Windows and macOS follow supporting-environment instructions.

picks.label: Geometry and simulation meshes
picks.reason: Geometry preparation, meshing and related workflow modules help prepare models for numerical solvers.
picks.tradeoff: A preprocessing platform does not replace the selected solver; module and package compatibility matter.

recipes.title: Process satellite imagery and environmental scenarios
recipes.description: Separate satellite preprocessing, scalable image algorithms, ecosystem-service models and general geographic editing.

picks.label: Sentinel product processing
picks.reason: Mission-specific toolboxes and processing graphs support remote-sensing raster workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Sensor product type and processing order matter; large scenes can require substantial memory and disk space.

picks.label: Scriptable image-processing algorithms
picks.reason: Command-line, Python and QGIS integrations suit repeatable processing of large remote-sensing imagery.
picks.tradeoff: Current package and QGIS-provider versions must match; ARM Mac usage follows a Docker route.

picks.label: Ecosystem-service scenarios
picks.reason: Models connect spatial land-use inputs with ecosystem-service indicators and scenario comparisons.
picks.tradeoff: Outputs depend on local data, assumptions and model scope; inspect the documented telemetry and data requirements.

picks.label: General desktop GIS
picks.reason: Broad vector and raster editing, geoprocessing and map production support the surrounding geographic workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Domain-specific satellite and ecosystem models may still require external tools or plugins.

recipes.title: Build an astronomy acquisition and analysis workflow
recipes.description: Acquisition, mount guiding, plate solving, image processing and time-series measurements are separate jobs that may need several tools.

picks.label: Automated acquisition on Windows
picks.reason: Sequences and supported equipment integrations organize deep-sky imaging sessions.
picks.tradeoff: Confirm the exact camera, focuser, mount and driver support; it is a Windows application.

picks.label: Mount guiding
picks.reason: Guide-star tracking, calibration and diagnostic tools help maintain tracking during exposures.
picks.tradeoff: Guiding cannot compensate for every mechanical or optical problem; the exact guide camera and mount need support.

picks.label: Plate solving and image inspection
picks.reason: Astrometric solving, stacking and FITS tools support image identification and processing.
picks.tradeoff: The selected star database, field of view and input quality affect solving; exact redistribution terms remain unverified.

picks.label: Astronomy image processing
picks.reason: Calibration, registration, stacking and processing tools turn acquired image sets into finished astronomical images.
picks.tradeoff: Correct calibration frames and acquisition metadata remain essential; it does not replace equipment-control software.

picks.label: Photometry and time-series measurements
picks.reason: Astronomy-focused ImageJ tools support calibrated image analysis and light-curve work.
picks.tradeoff: Photometric accuracy depends on calibration, apertures, comparison stars and timing metadata.

recipes.title: Create fonts and manage an installed font collection
recipes.description: Use a font editor to design glyphs and font behavior; use a manager to preview, activate and organize existing typefaces.

picks.label: Open-source font construction
picks.reason: Outline editing, font conversion and scripting cover a broad range of font-authoring tasks.
picks.tradeoff: The dense interface and production settings need learning; validate exports in target shaping and rendering engines.

picks.label: Approachable outline design
picks.reason: Vector glyph editing and common font exports provide a focused font-design workflow.
picks.tradeoff: The free binary edition restricts created fonts to SIL Open Font License output; commercial and advanced formats have separate editions.

picks.label: Commercial typeface production
picks.reason: Detailed glyph, family and variable-font tools target professional font production.
picks.tradeoff: It is paid Windows/macOS software; assess the trial against the required production workflow.

picks.label: Font activation across desktops
picks.reason: Previewing, collections and activation help manage working typeface libraries on Windows, macOS and Linux.
picks.tradeoff: Advanced Awesome features require payment, and application activation behavior needs checking.

picks.label: Linux desktop font management
picks.reason: Font previews, collections and fontconfig-oriented controls serve Linux desktop collections.
picks.tradeoff: Its scope is font management rather than glyph design; desktop and fontconfig behavior affect results.

recipes.title: Program instruments and perform with live code
recipes.description: Choose a beginner-facing live-coding instrument, visual patches or a deeper language for synthesis and precisely timed processes.

picks.label: Approachable live coding
picks.reason: An integrated code editor, samples and synthesis tools support musical programming and performance.
picks.tradeoff: Complex audio routing and custom DSP may require a lower-level environment; web and desktop distributions differ.

picks.label: Visual audio patches
picks.reason: A graphical dataflow model makes control, synthesis and interactive media patches explicit.
picks.tradeoff: External libraries and audio configuration can affect patch portability.

picks.label: Programmable synthesis systems
picks.reason: A language and synthesis server support algorithmic composition, instruments and flexible control.
picks.tradeoff: The language, server architecture and timing model take study.

picks.label: Detailed synthesis instruments
picks.reason: A large opcode library supports explicit signal processing and programmable instruments.
picks.tradeoff: Instrument design and host integration require technical learning; opcode support varies across environments.

picks.label: Precisely timed musical processes
picks.reason: Its strongly timed concurrent language makes timing and live program changes central to musical code.
picks.tradeoff: The timing and concurrency model is distinctive, and additional interfaces may require other tools.

recipes.title: Plan and write a novel, thesis or long document
recipes.description: Choose by working format and planning style: Markdown with citations, structured outlining, story development or a commercial project binder.

picks.label: Markdown research writing
picks.reason: Plain-text files, citation integration and export tools suit research notes and long Markdown documents.
picks.tradeoff: Advanced export depends on the external document toolchain and careful citation configuration.

picks.label: Open-source outlining
picks.reason: An outliner, story-planning tools and focused writing views support structured drafting.
picks.tradeoff: Export capabilities and platform packages differ from commercial writing suites; check the current package for the intended OS.

picks.label: Characters and story structure
picks.reason: Character, scene and narrative-planning tools keep story development alongside manuscript work.
picks.tradeoff: Community and Supporters editions have different features; optional synchronization is a separate service.

picks.label: Commercial project binder
picks.reason: Research material, scenes and draft organization share a project workspace with compilation tools.
picks.tradeoff: Windows and macOS licenses and features differ; learn compilation and backup behavior before a large project.

recipes.title: Translate documents or localize application strings
recipes.description: A translation-memory application fits documents; catalog editors fit software strings and localization formats.

picks.label: Document translation memory
picks.reason: Segmented translation, fuzzy matches, glossaries and translation memories support repeated document work.
picks.tradeoff: Check format filters and final exported documents; it is an assisted translation workflow rather than automatic translation alone.

picks.label: Focused localization editing
picks.reason: Catalog editing and validation support common software and website localization formats.
picks.tradeoff: Paid Pro assistance and services differ from the open-source core; verify the project format and plural rules.

picks.label: Integrated localization workflow
picks.reason: Translation-memory and project tools support sustained application localization work.
picks.tradeoff: Linux is the main desktop route; Windows and macOS installers offered by KDE are nightly testing builds.

recipes.title: Choose software for household books and spending records
recipes.description: Compare bookkeeping structure and import workflow before selecting a tool. Institution connectivity and financial-data formats vary.

picks.label: Double-entry books
picks.reason: Accounts, reconciliation, scheduled transactions and business-oriented records suit structured double-entry bookkeeping.
picks.tradeoff: The accounting model needs learning; online imports and quote services depend on external providers and components.

picks.label: Personal spending analysis
picks.reason: Imports, categories, budgets and reports make household transaction review approachable.
picks.tradeoff: It is oriented toward personal accounts rather than a full business ledger; third-party ports receive limited publisher support.

picks.label: Desktop personal-finance accounts
picks.reason: Account registers, scheduled transactions and reports organize household finances in a KDE application.
picks.tradeoff: Banking plugins vary by platform; the reviewed Windows distribution notes missing AqBanking support.

picks.label: Flexible transaction analysis
picks.reason: Category, tag and report tools support detailed inspection of imported spending records.
picks.tradeoff: Import quality and duplicate handling need review; non-Linux installation routes can require more setup.

recipes.title: Choose accessible input, screen reading and document reading
recipes.description: Match the barrier to the tool: eye-controlled typing, voice commands, desktop speech or accessible reading. Device and application compatibility determine the useful combination.

picks.label: Eye-controlled typing and pointer
picks.reason: An on-screen keyboard and communication tools support interaction through compatible eye trackers and other input methods.
picks.tradeoff: Confirm the exact tracker and OptiKey version; newer releases have changed support for some older hardware.

picks.label: Voice and alternative input
picks.reason: Voice commands, dictation and customizable input actions can support hands-free work across applications.
picks.tradeoff: Commands and recognition require setup and practice; Linux targets X11, and Talon+ has a separate paid membership.

picks.label: Linux desktop speech and braille
picks.reason: Orca exposes accessible desktop interfaces through speech and braille on supported Linux environments.
picks.tradeoff: Results depend on each application exposing a usable accessibility interface.

picks.label: Windows desktop screen reading
picks.reason: The existing NVDA record covers keyboard-driven screen reading and extensibility on Windows.
picks.tradeoff: Application accessibility, speech setup and add-on compatibility require individual checks.

picks.label: Accessible publication reading
picks.reason: Navigation and accessibility support focus on EPUB and other supported digital publications.
picks.tradeoff: Publication structure and protection schemes determine accessible reading; it does not replace a system screen reader.

recipes.title: Design page layouts and scalable artwork
recipes.description: Match the tool to page layout, vector illustration, everyday documents or programmable typesetting.

picks.label: Print layout
picks.reason: Page layout, color management and PDF output suit brochures and multi-page publications.
picks.tradeoff: Check imported assets and press requirements; proprietary layout-document interchange is limited.

picks.label: Vector artwork
picks.reason: SVG-native editing suits icons, logos and illustrations that must remain scalable.
picks.tradeoff: It is primarily a drawing workflow; complex multi-page publishing needs a layout application.

picks.label: Office documents
picks.reason: Writer, Calc and Impress cover ordinary documents without a separate publishing stack.
picks.tradeoff: Complex imported Office files and macros need compatibility checks.

picks.label: Programmable documents
picks.reason: The open-source compiler and templates support repeatable technical reports.
picks.tradeoff: The markup workflow and hosted-editor plans differ from traditional desktop word processing.

recipes.title: Inspect and process image files
recipes.description: Choose for RAW development, minimal viewing, broad browsing or repeatable image processing.

picks.label: RAW photography
picks.reason: Non-destructive processing and image-library tools fit photographic development.
picks.tradeoff: Learn the processing pipeline and verify camera support.

picks.label: Minimal viewing
picks.reason: A sparse viewer interface keeps attention on the image.
picks.tradeoff: It omits full cataloging and photo-editing features.

picks.label: Browse and batch
picks.reason: Viewing, metadata and batch conversion are available in one application.
picks.tradeoff: Company use needs an appropriate paid license.

picks.label: Scripted processing
picks.reason: Command-line transforms support repeatable conversion and image-composition pipelines.
picks.tradeoff: Build options, delegates and security policy affect supported formats.

recipes.title: Trim, convert and inspect media
recipes.description: Use the operation you need to choose between trimming, transcoding, container changes and technical inspection.

picks.label: Trim without full re-encoding
picks.reason: Stream-preserving cuts suit long recordings with unwanted sections.
picks.tradeoff: Keyframes constrain some cuts; store builds and direct-download pricing differ.

picks.label: Graphical conversion
picks.reason: An FFmpeg-based desktop interface exposes production-oriented conversion and rewrapping.
picks.tradeoff: Quality and delivery compatibility depend on the selected settings.

picks.label: Matroska tracks
picks.reason: Dedicated muxing and metadata tools manage tracks and chapters in MKV files.
picks.tradeoff: This does not replace a video-effects or general transcoding workflow.

picks.label: Diagnose a file
picks.reason: Reports codecs, tracks and technical properties before import or delivery.
picks.tradeoff: Inspection does not repair the file.

recipes.title: Create and time subtitles
recipes.description: Compare a broad subtitle-editing workflow with detailed styled subtitle typesetting.

picks.label: General subtitle work
picks.reason: Timing, conversion and video-assisted editing cover common subtitle preparation tasks.
picks.tradeoff: Runtime and media dependencies differ by platform.

picks.label: Styled typesetting
picks.reason: Audio timing, ASS styling and video preview support detailed subtitle placement.
picks.tradeoff: Player support for complex ASS styling varies.

recipes.title: Write music notation and guitar tabs
recipes.description: Choose among visual score entry, reproducible engraving and instrument-specific notation.

picks.label: Visual score editing
picks.reason: An open-source desktop score editor combines notation, playback and part extraction.
picks.tradeoff: The desktop app is distinct from paid score-sharing and optional sound services.

picks.label: Text-based engraving
picks.reason: Notation source can be versioned and compiled into printable scores.
picks.tradeoff: Learning the notation language is required.

picks.label: LilyPond editor
picks.reason: Editing aids and preview provide a focused environment for LilyPond projects.
picks.tradeoff: LilyPond remains a separate required engraving engine.

picks.label: Guitar tablature
picks.reason: Tablature and playback fit guitar-oriented composing and practice.
picks.tradeoff: Check import fidelity and the newer file format before sharing with older versions.

recipes.title: Build a software synthesis workspace
recipes.description: Compare modular patching, a broad hybrid synth and a focused FM instrument.

picks.label: Modular composition
picks.reason: Visual patching combines synthesis, sequencing and processing modules.
picks.tradeoff: Its workflow differs from a conventional linear DAW.

picks.label: Virtual modular rack
picks.reason: A module ecosystem and cable-based patching fit modular-synthesis study and sound design.
picks.tradeoff: Rack Free, Rack Pro and third-party modules have separate feature and licensing choices.

picks.label: Free hybrid instrument
picks.reason: Multiple synthesis methods and modulation options provide a broad sound-design palette.
picks.tradeoff: Plugin compatibility and complex-patch CPU demands need checking.

picks.label: FM specialist
picks.reason: DX7-inspired FM synthesis and patch workflows suit a specific sound-design approach.
picks.tradeoff: It is intentionally narrower than a general-purpose synthesizer.

recipes.title: Choose a personal knowledge base
recipes.description: Decide whether notebooks, local Markdown, hierarchical rich notes or plain-text sync integration best match your work.

picks.label: Open-source notebooks
picks.reason: Markdown notes, notebooks and several synchronization options suit a conventional research notebook.
picks.tradeoff: Hosted Joplin Cloud is optional and paid; test sync and restore behavior.

picks.label: Local linked files
picks.reason: Markdown vaults and links support a flexible, local-file knowledge graph.
picks.tradeoff: The app is proprietary; optional Sync and Publish services are paid.

picks.label: Rich hierarchy
picks.reason: Nested notes and multiple note types suit a structured personal knowledge base.
picks.tradeoff: Scripting and self-hosted options add administration responsibilities.

picks.label: Plain-text workflow
picks.reason: Markdown files and optional Nextcloud/ownCloud integration suit file-centered note management.
picks.tradeoff: The synchronization service is a separate component to configure.

recipes.title: Scan, search and organize paperwork
recipes.description: Choose a scanning interface, an automated OCR pipeline, or a focused page organizer.

picks.label: Scan to searchable PDF
picks.reason: Scanner acquisition, page handling and OCR are available in a desktop interface.
picks.tradeoff: Driver support and scan quality affect the result.

picks.label: Automated PDF OCR
picks.reason: A command-line workflow adds searchable text layers to existing scanned PDFs.
picks.tradeoff: Language packs, dependencies and OCR review are required.

picks.label: Organize pages
picks.reason: Merge, split, crop and reorder PDF pages interactively.
picks.tradeoff: It does not replace text editing or a redaction tool.

picks.label: Read and annotate
picks.reason: Document viewing and PDF annotation support reviewing the result.
picks.tradeoff: Annotation interoperability and platform packaging should be tested.

recipes.title: Analyze scientific images and simulation output
recipes.description: Match microscopy images, Python-based image stacks or simulation meshes to the appropriate analysis environment.

picks.label: Microscopy toolbox
picks.reason: The ImageJ distribution bundles many scientific imaging tools and plugins.
picks.tradeoff: Validate the chosen analysis and plugin versions before drawing conclusions.

picks.label: Python image stacks
picks.reason: Multidimensional viewing and Python integration fit custom scientific imaging workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Manage the Python environment, plugin versions and memory needs.

picks.label: Simulation visualization
picks.reason: Data readers and a visualization pipeline fit numerical and mesh-based simulation outputs.
picks.tradeoff: Large datasets and specialized formats require resource planning.

recipes.title: Map and process geospatial data
recipes.description: Choose a desktop map-making environment, analysis engine, terrain specialist or point-cloud pipeline.

picks.label: Desktop GIS
picks.reason: Map composition and spatial editing support a broad geographic-information workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Coordinate systems, data quality and plugins need review.

picks.label: Repeatable geospatial analysis
picks.reason: Dedicated raster/vector modules and scripting suit analytical processing.
picks.tradeoff: Region and projection concepts have a learning curve.

picks.label: Terrain specialist
picks.reason: Terrain, raster and geoscience modules support elevation-derived analysis.
picks.tradeoff: Check module behavior and version-specific file support.

picks.label: Point-cloud automation
picks.reason: Pipeline-based filtering and conversion suit batch LiDAR processing.
picks.tradeoff: A separate viewer helps inspect the results.

recipes.title: Design and simulate electronics
recipes.description: Compare complete PCB design, a structured component workflow, accessible prototype documentation and circuit simulation.

picks.label: PCB design suite
picks.reason: Schematic capture, board layout and 3D viewing cover a complete board-design workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Footprints and manufacturing outputs need checking against actual components and fabrication rules.

picks.label: Integrated component libraries
picks.reason: A consistent schematic/board/library model suits repeatable component-driven designs.
picks.tradeoff: Confirm library coverage and advanced board requirements.

picks.label: Prototype documentation
picks.reason: Breadboard, schematic and board views suit visually documenting accessible electronics projects.
picks.tradeoff: Official binaries are paid; component accuracy still needs review.

picks.label: Circuit simulation
picks.reason: A graphical front end connects schematics with several SPICE-compatible simulators.
picks.tradeoff: Models and simulator selection determine the validity of results.

recipes.title: Analyze tabular scientific data
recipes.description: Compare conventional statistics, Bayesian workflows, visual data mining and matrix-based numerical programming.

picks.label: Spreadsheet-style statistics
picks.reason: A graphical data editor and R-based analyses suit teaching and common statistical tasks.
picks.tradeoff: Choose the model and assumptions deliberately; extra modules may be required.

picks.label: Frequentist and Bayesian analysis
picks.reason: Graphical analysis and reporting cover both statistical approaches.
picks.tradeoff: Interpretation and study design remain the responsibility of the analyst.

picks.label: Visual analysis workflows
picks.reason: Connected widgets make exploratory analysis and machine-learning steps visible.
picks.tradeoff: Validate data splits and defaults to avoid misleading results.

picks.label: Numerical programming
picks.reason: Matrix-oriented syntax supports custom numerical experiments and plotting.
picks.tradeoff: Compatibility with MATLAB toolboxes and specialized integrations is incomplete.

recipes.title: Choose a graphical sequence-analysis and cloning workbench
recipes.description: Match the workbench to the laboratory task: broad sequence analysis, supported project workflows, or visual cloning design.

picks.label: Open graphical analysis workspace
picks.reason: Combines sequence viewing, annotation, alignment tools and visual workflows.
picks.tradeoff: External tools and reference databases add dependencies; validate each selected method.

picks.label: Supported integrated laboratory workflow
picks.reason: Brings mapping, alignment, cloning, automation and project management into a commercial desktop environment.
picks.tradeoff: Subscriptions, cloud entitlements and academic eligibility differ by plan.

picks.label: Visual cloning design and documentation
picks.reason: Plasmid maps, cloning simulation and edit history make construct design inspectable.
picks.tradeoff: Free Viewer mode supports inspection and annotation; full cloning design requires a paid subscription.

recipes.title: Create and inspect biological sequence alignments
recipes.description: Distinguish alignment computation from manual inspection. Difficult regions and biological assumptions still need review before tree inference.

picks.label: Scriptable alignment generation
picks.reason: Offers several sequence-alignment strategies and workflows for adding sequences to an existing alignment.
picks.tradeoff: Strategy choice and package licenses vary; inspect ambiguous alignment regions.

picks.label: Alignment interpretation with annotations
picks.reason: Links alignment editing and analysis with biological annotations and molecular structure views.
picks.tradeoff: Some services require a network connection, and external analyses have their own assumptions.

picks.label: Focused alignment inspection
picks.reason: Provides a dedicated viewer/editor with navigation suited to checking alignment columns and sequence labels.
picks.tradeoff: External aligners and Java packaging require separate setup.

recipes.title: Choose a phylogenetic inference method and interface
recipes.description: Choose by statistical question and workflow, then check models, support and uncertainty. These tools do not establish one universally best tree.

picks.label: Model-aware maximum likelihood
picks.reason: Combines maximum-likelihood inference, model selection, branch support and checkpointing.
picks.tradeoff: Alignment quality and model assumptions remain critical; complex models can consume substantial resources.

picks.label: Explicit scripted likelihood searches
picks.reason: Provides tree-search, parameter-optimization and bootstrap controls for reproducible analyses.
picks.tradeoff: Windows uses WSL; search replicates and settings must be justified.

picks.label: Graphical molecular-evolution analysis
picks.reason: Presents evolutionary distances and tree methods in an integrated graphical environment.
picks.tradeoff: Its no-charge terms are limited to research and education, with redistribution restrictions.

picks.label: Bayesian dated-tree models
picks.reason: Samples trees and parameters to represent posterior uncertainty in time-aware evolutionary models.
picks.tradeoff: Check priors, convergence, effective sample sizes and independent chains before interpretation.

picks.label: Display a legacy tree project
picks.reason: Provides branch/node display and annotation controls for tree figures.
picks.tradeoff: FigTree is superseded by PearTree; neither viewer replaces inference or convergence diagnostics.

recipes.title: Inspect reads, genome annotations and assembly graphs
recipes.description: Pick the data representation first: mapped reads, curated annotations, complex genome views or assembly-graph connectivity.

picks.label: Locus-level read and track review
picks.reason: Displays aligned-read and genomic-track evidence in a local desktop session.
picks.tradeoff: Large datasets need valid indexes and compatible reference coordinates.

picks.label: Extensible complex genome views
picks.reason: Supports a pluggable desktop workspace with multiple genomic representations.
picks.tradeoff: Plugins and input formats need preparation; the separate web deployment is a different product route.

picks.label: Genome annotation curation
picks.reason: Combines sequence-feature inspection with editing and comparative tools.
picks.tradeoff: Java and optional database workflows add setup requirements.

picks.label: Focused assembly and alignment viewing
picks.reason: Concentrates on visual review of sequencing assemblies and mapped reads.
picks.tradeoff: A visible pattern still needs an appropriate analytical method before drawing conclusions.

picks.label: Assembly-graph connectivity
picks.reason: Shows connections and branches that disappear in a flat contig file.
picks.tradeoff: Current packages differ by platform, and graph topology alone does not prove assembly correctness.

recipes.title: Inspect, preprocess and summarize sequencing quality
recipes.description: These tools cover complementary stages: diagnose raw reads, apply justified preprocessing, then compare results across samples.

picks.label: Per-file diagnostic reports
picks.reason: Reports sequencing quality and composition patterns before or after preprocessing.
picks.tradeoff: Warning thresholds are heuristics and can reflect legitimate assay properties.

picks.label: Preprocessing with recorded reports
picks.reason: Combines quality filtering, adapter trimming and HTML/JSON reporting in a scripted step.
picks.tradeoff: Trimming can remove useful sequence; tune settings for the actual library.

picks.label: Cross-sample report aggregation
picks.reason: Collects supported tool outputs into a project-level overview.
picks.tradeoff: It does not perform the underlying measurements; module recognition and sample naming affect aggregation.

recipes.title: Select a command-line tool for a genomic file operation
recipes.description: Choose by data model instead of treating every sequence utility as interchangeable.

picks.label: FASTA and FASTQ sequences
picks.reason: Filters, transforms, extracts and summarizes sequence records with self-contained executables.
picks.tradeoff: Check identifiers, strand handling and coordinate conventions.

picks.label: SAM, BAM and CRAM alignments
picks.reason: Sorts, indexes, filters and converts mapped-read alignment files.
picks.tradeoff: Reference and sorting assumptions must match downstream tools; Windows setup differs.

picks.label: Genomic interval relationships
picks.reason: Intersects, merges and compares regions such as genes, peaks and coverage intervals.
picks.tradeoff: BED and GFF coordinate conventions differ; current source and older docs also carry different license labels.

picks.label: Mapping long reads or assemblies
picks.reason: Aligns sequence data to a reference using task-specific presets.
picks.tradeoff: It is a mapper rather than a general file editor; this record verifies the published Linux binary route.

recipes.title: Choose a BIM authoring environment
recipes.description: Start with team deliverables, native operating-system needs, exchange formats and the authoring model.

picks.label: Revit-centered multidisciplinary delivery
picks.reason: Connects architectural, structural and building-services models with documentation.
picks.tradeoff: Native Windows requirement and separately licensed collaboration services can affect the toolchain.

picks.label: Architectural BIM on Windows or Mac
picks.reason: Combines architectural modeling, documentation and team workflows with native desktop options.
picks.tradeoff: Plan entitlements and consultant exchange requirements need agreement before a project starts.

picks.label: DWG-based transition into BIM
picks.reason: Places building-modeling and IFC tools alongside familiar DWG drafting workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Some integrations vary by OS; perpetual and subscription entitlements differ.

picks.label: Open IFC authoring inside Blender
picks.reason: Creates native IFC data with linked drawings, schedules and Python automation.

recipes.title: Review IFC deliverables and city-scale semantic models
recipes.description: A dedicated viewer suits reviewers who do not need a full authoring license. Check format coverage and paid extensions before selecting one.

picks.label: Focused IFC stakeholder review

picks.tradeoff: Optional plugins have separate licenses and the installer flow requests an email address.

picks.label: IFC, gbXML and CityGML review
picks.reason: Connects building-scale and city-scale semantic formats with property and relationship inspection.

picks.label: Review that may become IFC authoring
picks.reason: Native IFC editing can help when inspection uncovers data that must be changed.
picks.tradeoff: A Blender extension and alpha authoring workflow bring more setup than a standalone viewer.

recipes.title: Plan interior layouts and architectural concepts
recipes.description: Match the tool to the level of design detail: rooms and furniture, flexible spatial concepts or data-rich building models.

picks.label: Rooms and furniture
picks.reason: Links a floor plan with three-dimensional furniture placement and interior views.
picks.tradeoff: Free and paid distributions bundle different assets; it is not a full building-engineering system.

picks.label: Flexible spatial concept modeling

recipes.title: Choose a building-energy modeling workflow

picks.label: Commercial integrated performance analysis

picks.label: Existing DOE-2 project compatibility

recipes.title: Choose a lighting and luminaire planning tool

recipes.title: Choose a desktop life-cycle assessment workflow

picks.label: Graphical multi-database LCA work

picks.label: Brightway-connected analysis
picks.reason: Brings graphical project and inventory editing to the Python/Brightway ecosystem.

recipes.title: Choose CAD/CAM software for a CNC project

picks.label: Multiple fabrication processes

recipes.title: Arrange vector parts on sheet material

recipes.title: Choose software for preparing and sending laser jobs
recipes.description: Start with the controller, then decide whether integrated drawing, engraving preparation or a free focused sender is the priority.

picks.label: Free GRBL-focused Windows workflow
picks.reason: Prepares raster engraving jobs and sends them to compatible GRBL controllers.
picks.tradeoff: It is not a universal laser driver; verify the actual machine and material settings.

picks.label: Fabrication preparation in a browser
picks.reason: Can prepare laser jobs alongside milling and 3D-printing workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Generated jobs still require a compatible machine profile and sending/control route.

recipes.title: Measure a room, loudspeaker or live audio signal
recipes.description: Choose the measurement method before the interface. Calibrated microphones, sound-card routing and repeatable measurement conditions matter more than a polished plot.

picks.label: Room and loudspeaker response
picks.reason: Combines acoustic measurements, response views and equalizer-filter planning.
picks.tradeoff: Correct microphone calibration, timing and placement are required; an equalizer cannot repair every room problem.

picks.label: Live transfer-function workflow
picks.reason: Provides real-time spectrum, transfer-function and sound-level views.
picks.tradeoff: Sound-level accuracy depends on calibration and hardware; confirm platform pricing and distribution.

picks.label: Immediate signal inspection
picks.reason: Provides spectrum, spectrogram and scope views for an incoming audio signal.
picks.tradeoff: An attractive spectrum is not a calibrated room-acoustics report.

recipes.title: Reduce noise in an existing recording
recipes.description: These are conditional choices for recorded files or editor sessions. Compare the noise type, available edition and listening result on a copy of your source.

picks.label: Detailed restoration modules
picks.reason: Provides dedicated spectral and voice restoration workflows with noise-only monitoring.
picks.tradeoff: Module and standalone-editor availability vary by edition; strong processing can remove wanted speech.

picks.label: Editing with restoration in one workspace
picks.reason: Combines waveform/spectral editing with edition-specific restoration tools.
picks.tradeoff: Standard in-app tools differ from Premium/Ultimate plugins; Linux is currently a public beta.

picks.label: Restoration inside an Adobe audio session
picks.reason: Documents noise-print reduction, adaptive effects and spectral selection.
picks.tradeoff: Subscription licensing applies; offline Noise Reduction is specific to the Waveform Editor.

recipes.title: Choose a desktop audio-processing route
recipes.description: Match input versus playback processing, operating system and routing. Equalization, convolution and speech noise suppression solve different signal problems.

picks.label: Linux microphone and playback effects
picks.reason: Applies configured effects to PipeWire applications and can process microphone audio before the destination app.
picks.tradeoff: Install the selected noise plugin/model, keep hardware defaults as upstream instructs, and verify the destination receives processed input.

picks.label: Windows endpoint equalization
picks.reason: Provides configurable Windows audio processing for supported device paths.
picks.tradeoff: Driver and audio-mode compatibility determine whether processing applies; this record does not establish general-purpose noise suppression.

picks.label: Configured convolution and DSP pipeline
picks.reason: Offers explicit audio-processing pipelines for deliberate routing and filtering setups.
picks.tradeoff: Device backends and configuration require technical setup; measure the complete signal path.

recipes.title: Extract and inspect features from recorded audio
recipes.description: Use reproducible feature extraction when the question needs structured outputs, then review the visual or aligned result before interpreting it.

picks.label: Batch feature extraction
picks.reason: Runs supported audio-analysis plugins and writes machine-readable results.
picks.tradeoff: The selected plugin defines the measurement and may need separate installation or licensing.

picks.label: Detailed visual inspection
picks.reason: Displays and annotates recorded audio with layered analysis views.
picks.tradeoff: Plugin availability and parameter choices affect results; visual patterns need interpretation.

picks.label: Compare aligned recordings
picks.reason: Supports comparison of multiple audio recordings through an aligned visual workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Alignment is an analytical aid and can need correction; it does not prove musical or perceptual equivalence.

recipes.title: Inspect a monophonic vocal melody or speech contour
recipes.description: A singing-note transcription and a phonetic pitch analysis use different assumptions. Check octave errors and unvoiced regions against the recording.

picks.label: Correct an estimated melody transcription
picks.reason: Focuses on pitch and note extraction from monophonic recordings with manual correction.
picks.tradeoff: Polyphonic mixtures and ambiguous note boundaries require more work; automatic output is not ground truth.

picks.label: Speech-oriented acoustic analysis
picks.reason: Provides pitch, spectral and phonetic analysis with scripting.
picks.tradeoff: Pitch range, voicing assumptions and analysis windows must match the speaker and question.

picks.label: Layered listening and inspection
picks.reason: Lets analysts combine waveform, spectrogram and available analysis layers.
picks.tradeoff: Automatic feature extraction may require a suitable Vamp plugin.

recipes.title: Choose a photogrammetry reconstruction workflow
recipes.description: Select the intended output: camera poses, a textured object mesh, or a georeferenced aerial product. Capture overlap, scale control and validation remain essential.

picks.label: Camera reconstruction and sparse/dense stages
picks.reason: Provides graphical and command-line structure-from-motion workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Dense processing has hardware and dependency requirements; reconstructed scale needs external control.

picks.label: Dense mesh after camera registration
picks.reason: Consumes registered images and camera poses to produce dense geometry and textures.
picks.tradeoff: It needs an upstream registration stage and compatible interchange data.

picks.label: Aerial mapping through a web interface
picks.reason: The current WebODM distribution uses ODX for aerial imagery processing and offers official free installers.
picks.tradeoff: The current project is independent of OpenDroneMap; verify the actual engine and deployment route in older tutorials.

picks.label: Commercial integrated reconstruction
picks.reason: Combines reconstruction, inspection and project workflow in a commercial desktop product.
picks.tradeoff: Geospatial and advanced features depend on edition; check hardware and license requirements.

picks.label: Commercial desktop reconstruction route
picks.reason: Offers a photogrammetry pipeline for turning photographs into 3D assets.
picks.tradeoff: Revenue-based eligibility and entitlement terms need checking before assuming no-charge use.

recipes.title: Control a tethered camera from the computer
recipes.description: Check the exact camera model and requested control before selecting an application; USB detection alone does not prove live view or remote exposure support.

picks.label: Windows tethered still photography
picks.reason: Provides remote camera control and supported capture workflows on Windows.
picks.tradeoff: Individual camera models expose different capabilities.

picks.label: Linux tethering through supported cameras
picks.reason: Provides a graphical tethered photography workflow built around camera-control support.
picks.tradeoff: The underlying camera library and device support determine available actions.

picks.label: Frame-by-frame animation capture
picks.reason: Coordinates camera capture with animation review, exposure sheets and optional hardware.
picks.tradeoff: It is a paid production tool; supported camera and motion-control hardware must be checked.

recipes.title: Capture and assemble a stop-motion shot
recipes.description: Choose by the capture equipment and the production controls you need, then test one short shot with the real camera.

picks.label: Coordinated production set
picks.reason: Connects frame capture with exposure, dialogue, lighting and motion-control workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Hardware support and paid entitlements determine the usable feature set; the public FAQ currently links an older EULA.

picks.label: Open animation workspace with capture features
picks.reason: Combines 2D animation tools with supported stop-motion capture workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Camera integration and capture controls differ from a dedicated motion-control setup.

recipes.title: Prepare voice and mouth timing for animation
recipes.description: These tools address separate parts of dialogue production: generating a singing voice, timing phonemes and using those timings in an animation scene.

picks.label: Map recorded dialogue to mouth cues
picks.reason: Provides a focused phoneme and timing workflow for lip synchronization.
picks.tradeoff: Automatic or initial timing needs manual review and a matching mouth-shape set.

picks.label: Use dialogue timing in a 2D scene
picks.reason: Provides an animation environment for assembling character and scene work.
picks.tradeoff: Confirm supported timing interchange and drawing setup; import is not a finished performance.

picks.label: Synthesize a singing performance
picks.reason: Creates singing output from note and lyric data with supported voicebanks.
picks.tradeoff: Voicebank and renderer compatibility and licenses are separate; singing synthesis is not general dialogue lip-sync.

recipes.title: Choose support for a specific desktop access need
recipes.description: Select the access task first: pointer control, reading the interface, magnification or speech input. Verify the application combination with the person using it.

picks.label: Head movement for pointer control
picks.reason: Uses a camera-based head-tracking workflow to move the pointer.
picks.tradeoff: Camera placement, lighting and comfortable movement range affect usability.

picks.label: Windows screen reading
picks.reason: Provides spoken and braille access to supported Windows applications.
picks.tradeoff: Commercial licensing and application-specific accessibility support need checking.

picks.label: Windows magnification and reading support
picks.reason: Combines screen magnification with supported reading features.
picks.tradeoff: Edition and compatibility determine the available reading controls.

picks.label: Local speech/text workflows on Linux
picks.reason: Provides configurable speech recognition and synthesis routes through local models.
picks.tradeoff: Model downloads, hardware support and output quality vary; test the intended language and input device.

recipes.title: Read documents aloud and create personal speech audio
recipes.description: Choose the operating system, text workflow and voice first. The application license and the voice/output license are separate decisions.

picks.label: Windows reading with installed voices
picks.reason: Reads documents and clipboard text with supported Windows voices and can export audio.
picks.tradeoff: Noncommercial use is free; commercial organizations or paid audio distribution require the application license plus appropriate voice rights.

picks.label: Paid Windows reading workflow
picks.reason: Adds word highlighting, selected-text tools and batch audio creation.
picks.tradeoff: Optional Acapela voices are limited to NextUp products and personal generated-audio use unless separate rights are obtained.

picks.label: Configurable local Linux models
picks.reason: Combines text-to-speech with other local speech workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Model licensing, language support and hardware requirements differ from the application itself.

recipes.title: Choose an interface and solver route for CFD
recipes.description: Start from the physical model, mesh and verification plan. A friendlier interface does not validate turbulence, boundary conditions or convergence.

picks.label: Configurable open-source simulation toolkit
picks.reason: The Foundation distribution provides extensible finite-volume CFD workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Solver setup, meshing and scripting require expertise; other OpenFOAM distributions are separate products.

picks.label: Aerodynamic analysis and design research
picks.reason: Provides open-source simulation and adjoint-oriented design methods.
picks.tradeoff: Build features vary; documented prebuilt packages omit discrete-adjoint support.

picks.label: Graphical setup with commercial support options
picks.reason: Presents CFD preparation and analysis through a desktop interface with Windows, Linux and Apple Silicon Mac routes.
picks.tradeoff: The free edition is limited to 200,000 mesh cells and one CPU; paid terms and solver assumptions still matter.

recipes.title: Match a finite-element solver to the engineering problem
recipes.description: Compare the material models, coupling and preprocessing workflow required by the project. Benchmark a known case before interpreting a new model.

picks.label: Scriptable structural and thermal cases
picks.reason: Provides linear/nonlinear, static/dynamic and thermal analysis with an Abaqus-style input approach.
picks.tradeoff: A familiar input style does not guarantee complete Abaqus compatibility; geometry and solver checks remain necessary.

picks.label: Broad structural mechanics workflow
picks.reason: Combines structural analysis with the SALOME/AsterStudy ecosystem and scripted execution.
picks.tradeoff: Linux/container and third-party Windows packages have different installation and support boundaries.

picks.label: Multiphysics coupling
picks.reason: Offers a finite-element suite spanning multiple physical equations.
picks.tradeoff: Each coupled model needs suitable numerical settings and independent validation.

picks.label: Biomechanical constitutive models
picks.reason: Focuses on nonlinear mechanics and multiphysics used in biomechanics.
picks.tradeoff: Specialized material assumptions must match the specimen and loading; solver availability does not validate a biological conclusion.

recipes.title: Start or migrate an airfoil and wing analysis project
recipes.description: Potential-flow tools suit preliminary exploration under their model assumptions. Use more complete CFD only when its additional complexity is justified and validated.

picks.label: Current XFLR5-family starting point
picks.reason: Provides the successor workflow and recent releases for preliminary aerodynamic analysis.
picks.tradeoff: Version 7.58 ends Intel Mac binary packaging and the developer announces no future Linux packages; source builds and old binaries need a plan.

picks.label: Reproduce a legacy analysis
picks.reason: Preserves established airfoil and wing-analysis workflows and project compatibility.
picks.tradeoff: Development closed on 30 June 2026, so new projects should evaluate the successor.

picks.label: Broader CFD research route
picks.reason: Provides a solver and design framework for cases beyond the potential-flow workflow.
picks.tradeoff: It requires a suitable mesh, physical models and verification; it is not a drop-in file replacement.

recipes.title: Choose a water model for the actual hydraulic domain
recipes.description: A pressurized drinking-water network, sewer catchment, river floodplain and groundwater system require different governing models and inputs.

picks.label: Pressurized distribution network
picks.reason: Models hydraulic and water-quality behavior in drinking-water pipe networks.
picks.tradeoff: The Windows GUI and toolkit serve a specific network domain; input demands and calibration control the result.

picks.label: Stormwater and sewer catchments
picks.reason: Models rainfall-runoff, drainage networks and selected green-infrastructure controls.
picks.tradeoff: The official desktop GUI is Windows; a portable computational engine does not imply a matching native GUI.

picks.label: River and floodplain hydraulics
picks.reason: Provides river hydraulic analysis with official Windows desktop tools.
picks.tradeoff: Linux downloads are computational engines, not the Windows graphical application; the HEC software license is not open source.

picks.label: Groundwater flow and transport system
picks.reason: Provides the USGS modular numerical groundwater framework.
picks.tradeoff: Input preparation and conceptual-model design need separate tools and hydrogeological expertise.

recipes.title: Choose a molecular simulation engine
recipes.description: Select by force field, particle model, algorithms and required packages. An installed engine does not establish that the chosen model is scientifically appropriate.

picks.label: Molecular dynamics workflows
picks.reason: Provides a molecular-dynamics engine with documented build and acceleration options.
picks.tradeoff: Force-field preparation, sampling and validation dominate the scientific result; accelerator support depends on the build.

picks.label: Configurable particle interactions
picks.reason: Supports molecular and materials simulation through selectable interaction styles and packages.
picks.tradeoff: A prebuilt executable may omit a required package; record the exact build and configuration.

recipes.title: Inspect simulation particles, trajectories or molecular structures
recipes.description: Choose by data representation and analysis method, then keep visualization settings separate from measured quantities.

picks.label: Particle and atomistic analysis pipelines
picks.reason: Provides visualization and analysis workflows for particle-based simulation data.
picks.tradeoff: Basic and Pro capabilities differ; inspect the license and method requirements for the intended analysis.

picks.label: Molecular trajectory inspection
picks.reason: Provides molecular graphics and trajectory-oriented analysis for supported datasets.
picks.tradeoff: VMD has a custom source-available license, not an OSI open-source license; production and test builds differ by platform.

picks.label: Structures and experimental maps
picks.reason: Combines atomic models with density maps and related molecular data.
picks.tradeoff: Commercial-use conditions differ from free noncommercial use; trajectories and file formats need checking.

recipes.title: Choose a terrain-analysis working style
recipes.description: Begin with the DEM, coordinate system, resolution and drainage assumptions. Interface choice is secondary to preprocessing and interpretation.

picks.label: Graphical geoscientific toolbox
picks.reason: Offers dedicated terrain and raster-analysis modules.
picks.tradeoff: Processing choices and grid resolution can materially change derived landforms or drainage.

picks.label: Scripted local geospatial processing
picks.reason: Exposes terrain, hydrology and LiDAR tools through Python and R.
picks.tradeoff: Next Gen APIs and Python/R binary platforms differ; optional Pro workflows are separately licensed.

picks.label: Integrated raster/vector analysis system
picks.reason: Combines geospatial processing with reusable command-based workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Its data model and environment setup take time to learn.

picks.label: Map-centered desktop workbench
picks.reason: Combines data inspection, editing and access to processing providers.
picks.tradeoff: External provider availability and plugin versions determine which algorithms are actually installed.

recipes.title: Choose a network-analysis environment
recipes.description: A network picture and a biological interaction analysis require different supporting data. Check identifiers, directedness, weights and missing edges before comparing metrics.

picks.label: Interactive exploratory graph figures
picks.reason: Offers network layouts, filters, statistics and visual exports.
picks.tradeoff: The current roadmap still lists complete undo/redo as unfinished; save versions and avoid treating layout distance as scientific evidence.

picks.label: Attributed biological or research networks
picks.reason: Combines network visualization with data integration and an app ecosystem.
picks.tradeoff: App versions, identifiers and external services add dependencies and may have separate terms.

recipes.title: Clean a table or build a visual analysis pipeline
recipes.description: Choose an interactive cleanup tool for inconsistent values, or a workflow system when the analysis needs several repeatable processing stages.

picks.label: Inspect and normalize messy values
picks.reason: Facets, clustering and replayable transformations make table cleanup inspectable.
picks.tradeoff: Reconciliation can send selected data to external services; proposed merges need review.

picks.label: Reusable visual data pipelines
picks.reason: Connects preparation, modeling and optional code through a workflow graph.
picks.tradeoff: Desktop access is free, while Hub deployment/collaboration and some integrations have separate terms.

picks.label: Interactive exploratory analysis
picks.reason: Uses connected widgets for visual data analysis and machine learning.
picks.tradeoff: Widget choices and validation design determine whether model results are meaningful.

recipes.title: Choose an econometric and statistical workflow
recipes.description: Decide which model, diagnostics and reproducibility path you need before choosing the interface. None of these applications makes observational data causal by itself.

picks.label: Econometrics with GUI and scripts
picks.reason: Combines regression, time-series and panel methods with Hansl scripting.
picks.tradeoff: Statistical assumptions and model diagnostics remain the analyst’s responsibility.

picks.label: Programmable statistical environment
picks.reason: Offers broad statistical and graphical packages for scripted analyses.
picks.tradeoff: Package versions, methods and licenses need to be recorded separately.

picks.label: Syntax and graphical statistical workflow
picks.reason: Provides common data-analysis procedures through GUI and command syntax.
picks.tradeoff: Check procedure coverage and interchange compatibility for the specific study.

picks.label: Graphical frequentist/Bayesian analysis
picks.reason: Offers a graphical interface for documented statistical methods.
picks.tradeoff: Available analyses and prior settings must match the research question.

recipes.title: Choose a curve-fitting and plotting tool
recipes.description: Choose by model form, constraints, uncertainty and reporting needs. Residuals and parameter identifiability matter more than a smooth fitted line.

picks.label: Focused overlapping-peak fitting
picks.reason: Provides a dedicated interface for fitting peaks and experimental curves.
picks.tradeoff: Model choice and parameter constraints require domain judgment.

picks.label: Commercial integrated laboratory analysis
picks.reason: Combines fitting, statistics, graph formatting and reusable templates.
picks.tradeoff: Current native releases are Windows-only and advanced functions depend on edition and license.

picks.label: Open scientific plotting workspace
picks.reason: Combines imported data, plotting and fitting in a worksheet-oriented environment.
picks.tradeoff: Confirm the available fit model and interoperability with the lab’s data formats.

picks.label: Table-and-graph analysis workflow
picks.reason: Presents numerical data and scientific plots in a compact graphical workspace.
